highlight.title: BGP Vortex: New Internet Vulnerability Creates 37-Second Outages
highlight.summary: Security researchers discovered that <cite index="11-2,11-3">a BGP Vortex exploits widely used routing policies to trigger persistent oscillations between major Internet networks that can lead to Internet outages. 21/30 largest networks are susceptible to BGP Vortex attacks</cite>. <cite index="11-14">A single vortex could delay route propagation from almost instantaneous to up to 40 seconds, resulting in communication outages lasting approximately 37 seconds</cite>.

resources.title: What Happens When You Type a URL and Press Enter: The 2026 Edition
resources.why_now: Perfect for curious teens - explains the entire journey from typing a URL to seeing pixels on screen, covering DNS, HTTP/3, CDNs, and edge computing with real timing examples (200ms to 1.5 seconds for well-optimized sites).

resources.title: How DNS Works: Visual Guide
resources.why_now: A fun, colorful webcomic that explains DNS step-by-step - ideal for visual learners who want to understand how domain names become IP addresses without getting overwhelmed by technical jargon.

resources.title: The Complete DNS Guide 2026: Records, Setup & Troubleshooting
resources.why_now: Comprehensive technical resource covering DNS propagation (now 1-4 hours vs old '48 hour' myth), TTL settings, and real troubleshooting scenarios - essential for anyone managing websites or networks in 2026.

resources.title: Cloudflare Route Leak Incident: February 20, 2026 BGP Failure Analysis
resources.why_now: Real-world case study showing how BGP routing failures can make healthy systems unreachable for hours - demonstrates why understanding internet infrastructure matters even for application developers.

claude_take: <cite index="2-18,2-21">Submarine cables carry 99% of intercontinental Internet traffic</cite> yet most people think the internet is 'wireless' - understanding the physical infrastructure helps explain why BGP outages can be so devastating. <cite index="32-40,32-41">The internet in 2026 is faster, more encrypted, and more distributed than ever. HTTP/3 and QUIC are replacing the TCP connections that powered the web for decades</cite>, making networking knowledge more crucial as systems become more complex.
